Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems develops Cross-Domain Solution products that protect and defend the information flow of critical and time-sensitive data across military applications and networks. The Software Engineer will work in an agile development environment supporting the design, sustainment, and development of software, including SELinux policies, message parsers, XML schemas, network protocols, scripting, testing, and CI/CD activities.

Responsibilities
Supporting elements of the design/sustainment/development efforts
Duties to include software design and development in a Java/C++/C# SELinux environment, SELinux Policy creation, maintenance and debugging, message parser development, XML schema development, network protocol integration, shell scripting development, and software test
Provide software engineering
Flexibility and agility to changing requirements and programming languages, and a desire to learn and experience new opportunities to improve team performance is a must
The implementation of new stream and file pipelines for many different protocols including video
Development and test stories
Selloffs to track progress to a product owner
Volunteer support to the end customers by travelling to site and performing installations or trainings of the cross domain solution

The candidate should be a well-rounded software developer with experience in an object oriented language, such as C++, C# and Java
The candidate should be a self-starter that is attentive to details and works well in a team
Additionally, the proven ability to provide software engineering is required
Applicants selected will be subject to a government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information
The individual selected for this team will need to have a high level of self and team motivation
An ideal candidate will be a self-starter and a strong problem solver
They will also need to have a deep understanding of continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD)
The Cross domain solution also requires strong linux and networking knowledge
• DoD Interim Secret Security Clearance

For Washington state applicants only, non-represented full-time employees accrue at least 10 hours per month of Paid Time Off (PTO) to be used for incidental absences and other reasons and receive at least 90 hours for holidays.
For Washington state applicants only, represented full-time employees accrue 6.67 hours of Vacation per month, accrue up to 52 hours of sick leave annually, and receive at least 96 hours for holidays.
